title: Addressing Renovation Noise With a Neighbor
script: Neighbor Ibu Sri: [polite but tired] Pak Wawan, sorry to bother you at home, but the drilling from your renovation has been going on since six this morning.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [apologetic] I'm genuinely sorry about that, Ibu Sri. I honestly assumed the workers would start closer to eight, as we'd originally agreed.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [understanding] I don't mind renovations in general, everyone needs to fix their homes eventually, but the early hours are difficult for me.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [concerned] Do you work night shifts, by any chance? That would explain why early mornings matter so much to you specifically.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [explaining] Yes, exactly. I usually get home around five and finally fall asleep just before the drilling seems to start.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [regretful] I had no idea, otherwise I would have mentioned the schedule to you directly before any work began.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [reassuring] I appreciate you saying that. I'm not asking you to stop the renovation entirely, just to adjust the starting time slightly.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [thoughtful] That seems entirely reasonable. Would nine in the morning work better for your schedule, given how you described it?
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [relieved] Nine would honestly make a considerable difference. I'd have a few more hours of proper sleep before the noise begins.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [determined] Consider it done. I'll speak with the workers today and adjust their start time from tomorrow onward.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [grateful] Thank you, Pak Wawan. I know renovations already involve enough stress without adding neighborly disputes on top of everything.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [warmly] I'd rather know directly from you than have you quietly resenting the noise for the next two months.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [smiling] That's a fair way to think about it. How much longer is the renovation expected to take, roughly speaking?
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [estimating] About six more weeks, assuming nothing unexpected happens, which, admittedly, renovations rarely respect that assumption fully.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [laughing] That sounds about right from what I've heard from other neighbors who've renovated recently around here.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [sincere] I'll also let you know in advance whenever something particularly loud is planned, so it doesn't catch you off guard again.
Neighbor Ibu Sri: [appreciative] That would help enormously, honestly. Small warnings make inconveniences like this so much easier to plan around.
Neighbor Pak Wawan: [warmly] Consider it agreed then. Thank you for coming to talk instead of simply complaining to the building management first.

To ask him to stop renovating completely
quiz.explanation: She explains the drilling has been going on since six in the morning, which is difficult given her schedule.
